title: Wardley map tools: past and present
about: First read, public pages only, 22 Nov 2026. Positions are not given. Where no reason, date or price was visible it is recorded as not found. The tools named in the brief were checked: Online Wardley Maps and Mermaid exist and are read; others the scout found are added. The scout returned about 70 facts; 44 are kept here in condensed wording (duplicates and minor rows dropped), none changed in meaning.

findings.text: One text format is the hub of the open text-first tools: the Online Wardley Maps syntax (.owm) is read by its VS Code and Obsidian plugins, cli-owm, ipywardley (a subset) and wardleyToGo; Mermaid, Go-Wardley (HCL), wardleyToGo (WTG2) and the wmap tools each have their own syntax. Mermaid's wardley-beta uses explicit visibility and evolution coordinates. A converter exists (OWM to JSON, TOML, JSON Graph, Cypher) per the community list. So formats are many and interchange is thin.

Which stopped: a third-party listing marks five tools Discontinued, including three the scout read about (MapScript, Mapkeep, SharpCloud for Wardley use). Both MapScript and Mapkeep were hosted tools. NO reason is stated on any page read, so why they stopped is not known from this reading; any explanation would be a guess and none is offered here. The open text-first tools show no archive notice, but most dates were not visible.

Licences are mixed: MIT for the Online Wardley Maps editor, Mermaid, wardleyToGo, cli-owm and Excalidraw; copyleft for the Obsidian plugin (AGPL-3.0), ipywardley (GPL-3.0), Go-Wardley (MPL-2.0) and the wmap apps (GPLv3 and AGPLv3 per a list). What may be reused or merged depends on this; rights@ checks before any reuse.

In the pages read, no tool is described as keeping a map's history as dated steps played over time, or a source on every node; Mermaid has evolve arrows (movement) but no mention of sources or dated history. This is absence on the pages read, not proof, and the tools' own docs were not read in full; it is the one gap cartographer.d's design (history, sources) would fill, to verify before any claim.

Activity dates were mostly not visible in the fetches (commit and release dates absent for most repositories), the tools' own sites were unreachable for Map, Mapkeep and MapAware, and the AI-assisted creator (wardleymaps.ai) was read only as a listing. 'Still alive' and 'stopped' therefore rest on listings and absence of an archive notice, and need a second read with dates (the repository's commit page).
